items.title: OpenAI's first hardware product sounds more like a companion than a speaker
items.excerpt: OpenAI's debut hardware is shaping up to be a mobile, screenless smart speaker positioned as an always-present AI companion rather than a conventional device. Powered by GPT-Live, it will pack a camera and environmental sensors to read context and proactively anticipate needs throughout the day, with a rechargeable battery for portability. It is one of five hardware products in development under Jony Ive's LoveFrom, with the first device slated for 2027.

items.title: The OpenAI Mystery Device Will Reportedly Be Basically Just a Smart Speaker
items.excerpt: According to Bloomberg's sources, OpenAI's much-hyped device with Jony Ive will be a portable, battery-powered smart speaker with mechanical components that let it move, giving the impression of being 'alive.' The device aims to function as an AI companion that grows increasingly personalized and proactive over time. It faces steep skepticism given the revolutionary expectations Altman and Ive have set for it.

items.title: Neo robot hands breakthrough can build LEGOs, unzip jackets, and open a bag of Funyuns
items.excerpt: 1X has shown new dexterity demos for its Neo home humanoid, with the robot's hands building LEGO sets, unzipping jackets and opening snack bags. The fine-motor control marks a step toward the household chores 1X promises Neo will eventually handle autonomously via its Redwood AI model. The clips reignite both excitement and unease about capable humanoids entering the home.

items.title: Garmin Cirqa Smart Band launch: Garmin debuts a screen-free Whoop and Fitbit Air competitor
items.excerpt: Garmin has unveiled the Cirqa, a screen-free smart band that takes on Whoop and the Fitbit Air with subscription-free AI-driven health and sleep tracking. The wearable leans on Garmin's algorithms for recovery, readiness and coaching insights delivered through the app rather than an on-body display. It signals the growing category of minimalist, always-on AI health wearables.

items.title: Apple's smart glasses delay reportedly stems in part from major privacy concerns
items.excerpt: The Apple team behind its upcoming AI smart glasses is reportedly reworking the device around user-privacy safeguards, contributing to a delayed timeline. Apple is said to be exploring several tweaks so the camera-equipped, assistant-driven wearable handles bystander recording and data capture more responsibly than rivals. The glasses are now expected to be revealed at WWDC 2027.

items.title: Apple is banking on privacy to set its smart glasses apart
items.excerpt: Apple reportedly plans to differentiate its long-rumored AI smart glasses from Meta's Ray-Bans chiefly through privacy, exploring on-device processing and clearer recording indicators. The privacy-first engineering is said to be one reason the product slipped, with a reveal now expected next June at WWDC. The move frames privacy as Apple's central pitch as it enters the crowded AI-glasses race.

items.title: AMD's new X100 chip lineup puts embedded Ryzen AI 'Strix Halo' into robots
items.excerpt: AMD unveiled its X100 embedded APU lineup, putting Ryzen AI 'Strix Halo' silicon with Zen 5 CPU and RDNA 3.5 GPU cores into robots and other 'physical AI' machines. The chips are pitched as on-device brains for humanoids and edge devices, competing with Intel's Panther Lake and Nvidia's robotics platforms. It marks AMD's push into the emerging market for embedded edge-AI compute powering autonomous hardware.

items.title: Arctic Senza AI 370 review: Strix Point in a stealthy under-desk fanless design
items.excerpt: The Arctic Senza AI 370 is a fanless mini PC built around AMD's Ryzen AI 300-series 'Strix Point' APU with a dedicated NPU for on-device AI workloads. Its silent, under-desk-mountable chassis targets buyers who want local Copilot+-class AI acceleration without noise. The review weighs its NPU-driven capabilities against thermal limits of the passively cooled design.

items.title: Gemini for Home context memory expands to 15 mins, Nest Cam July 2026 update rolling out
items.excerpt: Google is rolling out new Gemini for Home capabilities, extending the assistant's context memory to 15 minutes so it can follow multi-step conversations across the smart home. A parallel Nest Cam firmware update accompanies the release. The upgrades push Google's generative AI deeper into everyday smart-home hardware and camera devices.

items.title: Honor Robot Phone leaked hands-on video shows thickness, camera gimbal in action
items.excerpt: A leaked hands-on video of Honor's 'Robot Phone' shows the device's added thickness and a motorized, gimbal-mounted AI camera that can physically move and track. Honor plans to showcase the AI-centric handset at WAIC in China on July 18. The unusual robotic form factor is Honor's bid to reimagine the smartphone as an active, agentic AI device.

items.title: New Tesla Optimus rival: Leak reveals first details about BYD's AI robot 'Xiao Di'
items.excerpt: EV giant BYD is reportedly preparing to unveil its own bipedal AI humanoid robot, called Xiao Di, positioning it as a rival to Tesla's Optimus. The robot is expected to make its public debut in August and could soon act as a sales assistant presenting EVs in BYD dealerships. It signals another major manufacturer entering the consumer-facing humanoid robot race.

items.title: OpenAI Is 'Very Interested' in Building Out ChatGPT Integrations for Wearables
items.excerpt: OpenAI President Greg Brockman signaled strong interest in bringing ChatGPT's increasingly 'Jarvis-like' AI agents to wearable hardware. He hinted at where the company's agentic assistants could head next and in what device forms, beyond the rumored screenless companion speaker. The comments underline OpenAI's ambition to embed ChatGPT into always-available, on-body AI devices.

items.title: My Life With Looki Is a Harbinger of Always-On Recording Glasses to Come
items.excerpt: CNET's Scott Stein lives with Looki, an almost always-on camera-equipped AI pendant that continuously captures and recalls your day. The wearable embodies the extreme assistive aspirations of memory-logging AI, while surfacing the social discomfort and privacy tension of persistent recording. Stein frames it as a preview of the always-on recording glasses and pendants arriving next.

items.title: Samsung Unveils More Smart Glasses Designs from Gentle Monster & Warby Parker
items.excerpt: Samsung teased a fresh slate of Android XR smart-glasses designs, including new frames from eyewear partners Gentle Monster and Warby Parker. The Gemini-powered glasses, developed jointly with Google, expand the style options ahead of a wider release. The reveal fleshes out Samsung and Google's push to make AI smart glasses look like everyday eyewear.
